HD Graphics Updating Clientele Branding Using Extensions

Client demand handed HD Graphics a daunting quarter: refresh a dozen legacy brands without letting quality or storytelling slip. This partner story walks through how the team used Graphic Net's extension toolkit to align art direction, automate the compliance checks, and still leave room for the custom work clients actually remember.

The art direction alignment happened before any asset was touched. For each of the twelve brands, the team encoded the refreshed direction as a Net.0 rule set: palettes, type scales, logo treatments, and layout grids. Extensions then audited every existing asset against the new rules and produced a ranked worklist, so the studio knew on day one which brand had two hundred violations and which had nine.

Compliance automation carried the volume. A custom extension re-rendered template-driven assets against the new rule sets automatically, clearing the bulk of each worklist without a designer opening a file. Assets that failed automated refresh, the genuinely bespoke pieces, routed to the design team with the specific rule violations annotated, which cut review rounds roughly in half.

The custom storytelling stayed human on purpose. Hero campaigns, founder pages, and signature illustrations were explicitly exempted from automated refresh and rebuilt by hand within the new direction. The extension toolkit's job was to clear the routine work fast enough that the team had the hours to do that bespoke work properly.

All twelve refreshes shipped inside the quarter, and the rule sets remain live as guardrails for every future asset. The next refresh, the ops lead notes, will be a rule-set edit rather than a project.



  • Brand Builder Magazine:
    - Twelve Brands, One Quarter: Inside a Bulk Refresh
  • Partner Playbook Press:
    - Encoding Art Direction as Enforceable Rules
